chunks: Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
The obligatory tawaf, if you add to it, is like salat; so when you add to it, repetition is required of you. And likewise is the sa'y.

key_terms.السَّعْيُ: the ritual walking between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat, used here as a legal analogy for invalidating addition
key_terms.الطَّوَافُ: the ritual circumambulation of the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repetition of the act due to invalidity
key_terms.الْمَفْرُوضُ: that which is obligatory and legally prescribed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs more than the prescribed number of circuits in obligatory tawaf or sa'y?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding excess in obligatory tawaf and sa'y during hajj rites. It states that adding to the prescribed amount invalidates the act in a manner comparable to salat, requiring its repetition.
